The only read operation that may preserve the original timestamp is the file-move response itself. I will re-express the move results and original files with their full metadata, then inspect the timestamps without attempting to deserialize them.

```python
original_file_metadata = [apis.file_system.show_file(access_token=file_system_access_token, file_path=path) for path in vacation_files]
moved_file_metadata = [apis.file_system.show_file(access_token=file_system_access_token, file_path=path) for path in [result['destination_file_path'] for result in vacation_move_results]]
metadata_summary = {
    'original': [item['path'] for item in original_file_metadata],
    'moved': [item['path'] for item in moved_file_metadata],
    'original_created_at': [item['created_at'] for item in original_file_metadata],
    'moved_created_at': [item['created_at'] for item in moved_file_metadata],
}
print(metadata_summary)
```
